svg.title: Landlord Pitch Gates for Rental Arbitrage
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-landlord-pitch-gates; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Landlord Pitch Gates for Rental Arbitrage; subtitle: Framing, rent cap, landlord fears, and proving unit one; caption: Four gates distilled from operators who pitched hundreds of landlords, including Aurelio Licata's 500+ pitches that produced 50+ properties.; assumptions note: The $2,000 rent against $3,000 charged is Sean Rakidzich's baseline spread rule; Linda Kim's $4,000 ask against a $3,700 need is a single walk-away example.; note: Drawn from Aurelio Licata (Q3hSpjquUTE), Rafa Loza (894g1JF-IuM), Sean Rakidzich (lGwvDjwR4uU), Linda Kim (5vV0oy-jJ7g), Jorge Contreras (_M0OdXelhoU), and LoCasa (OSi_ARPIpaM).; nodes: gate: G1; question: Did the pitch open as a corporate housing company with the filter question about short-term furnished leases?; pass next: G2; fail action: Reframe; never lead with Airbnb, and ask whether the landlord allows leases for short-term furnished housing.; gate: G2; question: Is the rent low enough to charge roughly double, such as $3,000 against $2,000 rent?; pass next: G3; fail action: Walk away, as Linda Kim did from a $4,000 ask against a $3,700 need.; gate: G3; question: Are on-time rent and property condition answered with autopay two days early and written damage responsibility?; pass next: G4; fail action: Show the autopay confirmation itself instead of arguing the point.; gate: G4; question: Is unit one profitable before adding unit two?; pass next: Sign a two-to-three-year lease under an LLC and bind your own liability and loss-of-income coverage.; fail action: Fix unit one first; adding more units does not solve the problem.

text.title: Landlord Pitch Gates for Rental Arbitrage
text.tspan: Landlord Pitch Gates for Rental Arbitrage

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Did the pitch open as a corporate housing company with the filter question about short-term furnished leases?; pass next: G2; fail action: Reframe; never lead with Airbnb, and ask whether the landlord allows leases for short-term furnished housing.

gate: G2; question: Is the rent low enough to charge roughly double, such as $3,000 against $2,000 rent?; pass next: G3; fail action: Walk away, as Linda Kim did from a $4,000 ask against a $3,700 need.

gate: G3; question: Are on-time rent and property condition answered with autopay two days early and written damage responsibility?; pass next: G4; fail action: Show the autopay confirmation itself instead of arguing the point.

gate: G4; question: Is unit one profitable before adding unit two?; pass next: Sign a two-to-three-year lease under an LLC and bind your own liability and loss-of-income coverage.; fail action: Fix unit one first; adding more units does not solve the problem.

text.title: Assumptions: The $2,000 rent against $3,000 charged is Sean Rakidzich's baseline spread rule; Linda Kim's $4,000 ask against a $3,700 need is a single walk-away example.
text.tspan: Assumptions: The $2,000 rent against $3,000 charged is Sean Rakidzich's baseline spread rule; Linda Kim's $4,000 ask against a $3,700
need is a single walk-away example.
